chunks: Do those who seek evil think that We shall make them equal in life and death to those who believe and do good? How bad is the judgement that they make!
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the fate of evildoers and the righteous in this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Jathiya refutes the egalitarian assumption of polytheists that their worldly success equates to spiritual merit, emphasizing that divine justice distinguishes between the righteous and the wicked in both life and death. It underscores the concept of 'Haqq al-Nas' and individual accountability, critiquing those who judge by superficial metrics rather than the depth of their faith and deeds. The verse serves as a reminder that the 'evil deeds' (Sayyi'at) are not merely actions but a state of being that precludes the equality of the believers.
